\textbf{\bn{সন্দেহ} \bn{করা}} — \emph{sôndeh kôrā} — \textquotedblleft{}to doubt\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{সন্দেহ} \bn{করা}} (\emph{sôndeh kôrā}) is \emph{sôndeh}, \textquotedblleft{}doubt\textquotedblright{}, Sanskrit \emph{saṁdeha} taken over whole, + \emph{kôrā}, \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{}, from Sanskrit \emph{karoti}, \textquotedblleft{}does\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 2814).
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{হাঁচা} (hā̃chā)}{হাঁচা (hā̃chā)}]{\bn{হাঁচা} (hā̃chā) — to sneeze}

\label{lesson:BN-C150-hacha}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to argue, then the Bengali for to carry on.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{হাঁচা}}
\textbf{\bn{হাঁচা}} — \emph{hā̃chā} — \textquotedblleft{}to sneeze\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{হাঁচা}} (\emph{hāṁchā}) goes back to Sanskrit \emph{hañji}, \textquotedblleft{}sneezing\textquotedblright{}. CDIAL gives no Bengali form under that entry, but it lists Assamese \emph{hāṁci}, \textquotedblleft{}sneezing\textquotedblright{}, the forms nearest to Bengali (CDIAL 13941a). CDIAL notes that the Sanskrit word is thought to be imitative.
\end{cousinweb}
